texts.preamble: Amrit Lal Makhija vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2019 Author: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava Bench: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava
texts.facts: As per prosecution case is that on 08.04.2008 committee constituted by District Administration along with SDM Gohalpur has inspected Murli Dairy situated at Kandra Kheda Pariyat Jabalpur where applicant found present. On asking about the license same was not produced by the applicant. On the suspicious of adulteration of milk, the committee has purchased 1500 ml milk from applicant Amrit Lal Makhija vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170877499/ 1 and same were sealed as per procedure. Pnachnama has also been prepared and same was duly signed by witnesses. The sample were sent to Public Analyzer, State Food Laboratories, bhopal for analysis. The part of sample has also been sent to Local Health Officer, Jabalpur. On 14.07.2008, a report has been received from Deputy Director Food and Drug Administration and according to it the sample which was seized from the possession of present applicant is found adulterated. L e a r n e d counsel for the applicant/accused submits that 2 CRR-4317-2019 applicants/accused are innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this case. He is in jail since 27.08.2018.
texts.arguments: He further submits that both the Courts below erred in convicting the applicant whereas there is no offence is made out against him. It may be seen that from the record that the sample was taken on 08.04.2008 and the public analyst has dispatched his report on 14.05.2008. Thereafter, the complaint case filed on 21.08.2008 after passing more then 4 months from taking sample. He further submit that the self life of the milk is not more than three months under refrigerating condition. In the present case, the complaint itself was filed beyond the reasonable period, applicant can not be held guilty. He further submits that the Food Inspector did not homogenize the milk while taking it sample and because of it the milk fat was found deficit in the milk. The applicant has a license which was expired on 31.03.2008 i.e. 8 days prior to the inspection and applicant has already applied for its renewal. These fact was overlooked by the learned Appellant Court and convicted the applicant. The prosecution has failed to proved its case even then both the Courts have convicted the applicant. If the applicant is not released on bail, the purpose of filing this application will be frustrated. Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the applicant may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail. In support of his contention he has relied the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan passed in Criminal Appeal No. 214-2015/2016. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the application.
